Bartleby, The Scrivener

A STORY OF WALL-STREET.

by Herman Melville




I am a rather elderly man. The nature of my avocations for the last
thirty years has brought me into more than ordinary contact with what
would seem an interesting and somewhat singular set of men, of whom as
yet nothing that I know of has ever been written:—I mean the
law-copyists or scriveners. I have known very many of them,
professionally and privately, and if I pleased, could relate divers
histories, at which good-natured gentlemen might smile, and sentimental
souls might weep. But I waive the biographies of all other scriveners
for a few passages in the life of Bartleby, who was a scrivener of the
strangest I ever saw or heard of. While of other law-copyists I might
write the complete life, of Bartleby nothing of that sort can be done.

巴特尔比，抄写员

华尔街的故事

赫尔曼·梅尔维尔




我是一个年纪相当大的人了。过去三十年来，我的职业性质使我比常人更多地接触到一类看似有趣且颇为特殊的人，据我所知，至今还没有人写过关于他们的文字——我指的是法律抄写员或者说誊写员。我在职业上和私人生活中认识过很多这样的人，如果我愿意，可以讲述各种各样的故事，善良的绅士们听了会微笑，多愁善感的人听了会流泪。但我要放弃其他所有抄写员的传记，只讲述巴特尔比生平中的几个片段，他是我见过或听说过的最奇特的抄写员。对于其他法律抄写员，我或许可以写出完整的生平，但对于巴特尔比，却无法做到这一点。

Bartleby, the Scrivener

A Story of Wall Street

Herman Melville




I am a rather elderly man. The nature of my avocations for the last thirty years has brought me into more than ordinary contact with what would seem an interesting and somewhat singular set of men, of whom as yet nothing that I know of has ever been written:—I mean the law-copyists or scriveners. I have known very many of them, professionally and privately, and if I pleased, could relate divers histories, at which good-natured gentlemen might smile, and sentimental souls might weep. But I waive the biographies of all other scriveners for a few passages in the life of Bartleby, who was a scrivener the strangest I ever saw or heard of.
